questions.problem:
The matrix $Q$ is given below. Let ${q}_{1}$, ${q}_{2}$, and ${q}_{3}$ be the respective columns of $Q.$ Determine if $B=\text{{}{q}_{1},{q}_{2}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(Q).$ If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$, where ${q}_{3}={x}_{1}{q}_{1}+{x}_{2}{q}_{2}.$

$$
Q=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 8 \\ -3 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $Q$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}Q & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 8 \\ -3 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 8 & 24\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{8}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(Q)$ is $\{{q}_{1},{q}_{2}\},$ that is to say,

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\}.
$$

Now, since the $3$rd column of the reduced matrix is a non-pivot column, then the entries in that column tell us the coefficients needed to express ${q}_{3}$ as a linear combination of all the other columns in the original matrix. So, we have

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{q}_{3}}={{(2)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{q}_{1}}+{{(3)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{q}_{2}}.
$$

This gives us ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=2\cdot 3=6.$

questions.problem:
The matrix $Q$ is given below. Let ${q}_{1}$, ${q}_{2}$,  ${q}_{3}$ and ${q}_{4}$ be the respective columns of $Q.$
Determine if $B=\text{{}{q}_{1},{q}_{4}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(Q).$ 
If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{4}$, where ${q}_{3}={x}_{1}{q}_{1}+{x}_{4}{q}_{4}.$ 

$$
Q=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 & -30 & -15 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 & 24 & 14\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $Q$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}Q & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 & -30 & -15 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 & 24 & 14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=(-\frac{1}{5}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 6 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 & 24 & 14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 6 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 6 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 6 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $4$th columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(Q)$ is $\{{q}_{1},{q}_{2},{q}_{4}\}.$ 

So, we conclude that $B=\{{q}_{1},{q}_{4}\}$ is not a basis of $\text{Col}(Q).$

The matrix $T$ is given below. Let ${t}_{1}$, ${t}_{2}$, and ${t}_{3}$ be the respective columns of $T.$ Determine if $B=\text{{}{t}_{1},{t}_{2}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(T).$ If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$, where ${t}_{3}={x}_{1}{t}_{1}+{x}_{2}{t}_{2}.$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 8 \\ 3 & 8 & 30\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $T$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 8 \\ 3 & 8 & 30\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(T)$ is $\{{t}_{1},{t}_{2}\},$ that is to say,

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 8\end{aligned}]\}.
$$

Now, since the $3$rd column of the reduced matrix is a non-pivot column, then the entries in that column tell us the coefficients needed to express ${t}_{3}$ as a linear combination of all the other columns in the original matrix. So, we have

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 30\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{t}_{3}}={{(2)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{t}_{1}}+{{(3)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 8\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{t}_{2}}.
$$

This gives us ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=2\cdot 3=6.$

questions.problem:
The matrix $V$ is given below. Let ${v}_{1}$, ${v}_{2}$,  ${v}_{3}$, and ${v}_{4}$ be the respective columns of $V.$ Determine if $B=\text{{}{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\text{}}$ is a basis of $\text{Col}(V).$ If that is the case, find ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$, where ${v}_{4}={x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}.$

$$
V=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 1 & -2 & -3 & -3 \\ -2 & 6 & 8 & 12\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $V$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 1 & -2 & -3 & -3 \\ -2 & 6 & 8 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & -6 \\ -2 & 6 & 8 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & -6 \\ 0 & 6 & 6 & 18\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 6 & 6 & 18\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-6){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we see that the pivot columns are the $1$st and $2$nd columns. So, a basis of $\text{Col}(V)$ is $\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\},$ that is to say,

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 6\end{aligned}]\}.
$$

Now, since the $4$th column of the reduced matrix is a non-pivot column, then the entries in that column tell us the coefficients needed to express ${v}_{4}$ as a linear combination of all the other columns in the original matrix. So, we have

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3 \\ 12\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{v}_{4}}={{(3)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{v}_{1}}+{{(3)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{v}_{2}}.
$$

This gives us ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=3\cdot 3=9.$
